questionText: What is statelessness in REST and why does it matter?

target.learningOutcome: The learner can distinguish conversational session context from stored resource state, explain why each request must stand on its own, and model a multi-step workflow as an explicit resource.
outOfScope: The false claim that a stateless server stores no data
The false claim that REST requires JWT

claims.statement: REST statelessness requires each request to contain the information needed to understand it without depending on server-stored conversational context from earlier requests.
The stateless constraint does not forbid resource data, users, permissions, caches, transactions, or workflow records from being stored by the server.
A request can present an authorization credential such as an OAuth bearer token; REST statelessness does not require that credential to be a JWT.
Removing hidden per-client conversational context improves request visibility, reliability after process failure, and the ability to route requests among server instances.
A multi-step workflow can preserve business progress as an explicitly identified resource so the next request does not depend on one process remembering an invisible session step.

examples.title: Create and retrieve an explicit checkout resource

validation.command: Parse both HTTP/1.1 request lines, Host and Authorization fields, JSON body, 201 status line, and Location field with the focused REST-foundations validator
validation.expected: The later request identifies checkout CH-21 and carries a bearer credential without relying on the first server process

visuals.title: State that may remain and context that must travel

notes: Do not promise automatic scalability; statelessness removes one routing dependency but does not solve shared storage, contention, or capacity.

review.notes: The stateless constraint was checked against Fielding and bearer-token transport against RFC 6750. The HTTP and JSON example passed mechanical parsing. The state comparison remains awaiting rendered editorial review before approval.
